HARKESH MANUJA, J. (ORAL)

The appellants / State of Haryana, by instituting the present appeal preferred under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short "the Act"), are seeking setting aside of the award dated 14.01.1998 passed by learned Additional District Judge, Hisar (hereinafter to be called as "Reference Court"), while restoring the "Reference Court award dated 28.02.1995 2 passed by the Land Acquisition Collector, PWD B&R Branch, Hisar (for short "LAC LAC").
[2] In pursuance of Haryana Govt. Notification under Section 4 of the Act issued on 25.05.1994,,
followed by Notification dated 26.08.1994 6.08.1994 under Section 6 thereof, land measuring 0.46 acres, including the land of respondents,, situated in revenue estate of Village Hindwan, Hindwan Tehsil & District Hisar, was acquired.
The public purpose for acquisition of the land was stated to be "Construction of 1 of 3 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:086482 link road from Village Hindwan to Kurari Shahpur in Hisar".

The LAC, vide Award No. 3-H, dated 28.02.1995, assessed the market value of acquired land @ Rs. 84,000/- per acre for Nahri land, while Rs.40,000/- per acre for Tal land alongwith other statutory benefits.

Ultimately, the cost of land worked out by the LAC, is as State Of Haryana vs Sher Singh Etc on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39626679/

[3] Dissatisfied with the aforesaid Award, landowners / interested persons filed objections under Section 18 of the Act,
which were decided vide award dated 14.01.1998 by Reference Court, whereby the market value of the acquired land was enhanced / assessed by doubling the amount as awarded by LAC, i.e. Rs.59,650/- (Rs. 29,825 x 2), besides granting other statutory benefits.
Hence, the present appeal.

[4] Impugning the aforesaid award dated 14.01.1998 passed by Reference Court, learned counsel for the appellants-State submits that the assessment of compensation has been made by Reference Court purely on the basis of guess work and the same is not based on any evidence available on record and thus, the award becomes unsustainable.
[5] After hearing learned counsel for the appellant-State of Haryana and having gone through the paper-book / relevant records, I am unable to find substance in the submissions made on behalf of the appellant.
2 of 3 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:086482 [6] In the present case, though the enhancement has been awarded in favour of the respondents-landowners on the basis of thumb rule; however, a perusal of the record shows that the landowners in their evidence produced sale deed dated 28.08.1992 (Ex. P-1), pertaining to 64 kanals 2 marlas of land situated within the same revenue estate and the sale consideration therein was @ Rs.8,00,000/-, thereby making it approximately Rs.
1,00,000/- per acre.

The aforesaid sale-deed was though ignored by the Reference Court merely for the reason that the vendors or vendees were not got examined to prove the same, which, in the humble opinion of this Court, was against the settled canons of law.

In such circumstances, in case the Reference Court could have relied upon the sale deed dated 28.08.1992 (Ex. P-1), wherein the sale consideration was around rupees one lakh per acre, the determination of compensation in favour of the respondents-landlords @ Rs. 59,650/- cannot, by any stretch of imagination, be held on the higher side.
[7] Consequently, finding no merit in the present appeal, the same is hereby dismissed.
[8] Pending miscellaneous application(s), if any, shall also stand(s) disposed off.
July 09, 2024 ( HARKESH MANUJA )
'dk kamra' JUDGE
